newsitem.title: USA: Philips venture frees Lucent - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Philips venture frees Lucent - analysts.

text.p: The consumer products venture of Philips Electronics NV and Lucent Technologies Inc strengthens Philips' U.S. product-marketing foothold and frees Lucent to focus on its network infrastructure businesses.

After news of the joint venture, announced earlier on Tuesday, Lucent shares rose nearly four percent to 70-3/8 at midday, a gain of 2-1/2. Philips shares ended the trading day in Amsterdam up 7.90 guilders at 128.90, a gain of 6.5 percent.
"Three of Lucent's four main businesses are absolute home runs," SBC Warburg analyst Barry Sine said of Lucent's network systems, business communications and semiconductor operations.
"One of them -- consumer products -- is more of a question mark," Sine said. "This deal puts Lucent's consumer products business on more of a strategic footing," he said.

"This is very positive. It again shows that the Lucent management team is focused on increasing shareholder value and allows it to really be a pure-play infrastructure provider," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Jim Parmelee agreed.

Sine said the new venture, which will operate under the name of Philips Consumer Communications both overseas and in the United States, will lift Philips' consumer marketing profile in the United States.

"This is a great opportunity to build on the old AT&T business to establish a great presence in the United States," Sine said of plans to merge Lucent's consumer operations with Philips. Lucent is the former equipment arm of AT&T Corp.

Sine said Philips' brand identity in the United States -- Philips Magnavox -- reflects the ignorance U.S. consumers have of the Dutch electronics company. "U.S. consumers think Philips is the first name of the Magnavox founder," he joked.
Parmelee rates Lucent stock a buy. Sine has a hold rating based on valuation concerns. Lucent stock was trading at a historic high Tuesday, exactly double its price a year ago.

Lucent's consumer products business, which operates in an industry growing at low double-digit rates, has suffered from modestly declining revenues as the old AT&T business of renting phones to customers has receded, an official said.

In a conference call, Carly Fiorina, the president of Lucent's existing consumer products business, said the revenue decline also reflected the closure of Lucent phone center stores and the pruning of certain product lines.
The consumer products business has acted as a drag on the other three core businesses of the company, which are growing in the 20 percent range, Sine said.
Still, the Lucent business operates at a modest profit, company officials told Wall Street analysts in a conference call with reporters Tuesday.

"This joint venture will be profitable from day one," said Michael McTighe in the same conference call. McTighe is the managing director of Philips' existing consumer electronics business and chief executive of the new venture.
